notes: The source's own document deliberately spans a full liturgical year across two calendar years, titled 'Last Sunday after Pentecost, 2025 – Advent I, 2026' on its own cover line: it opens with the week of November 23, 2025 (Christ the King) and closes with the week of November 22, 2026 (also Christ the King, the Sunday immediately before Advent I 2026). Per this corpus's existing precedent for a source whose own declared range spans a year boundary (episcopal-california-2026.json), the entries that fall before January 1, 2026 are included in this '-2026' file rather than split out or dropped.

The source's own printed year is wrong for eleven of its 53 entries, verified against the real day-of-week for each printed month/day (every entry in this cycle is a Sunday). The five entries headed 'The week of November 30, 2026' through 'The week of December 28, 2026' are printed with year 2026, but November 30 / December 7 / 14 / 21 / 28 are Sundays only in 2025 (they fall on a Monday in 2026) -- corrected here to 2025, which also makes them fall immediately before the January 4, 2026 entry that follows (itself printed correctly and a real Sunday). Symmetrically, the six entries headed 'The week of October 18, 2025' through 'The week of November 22, 2025' are printed with year 2025, but October 18 / 25 and November 1 / 8 / 15 / 22 are Sundays only in 2026 (they fall on a Saturday in 2025) -- corrected here to 2026, continuing directly from the October 11, 2026 entry that precedes them. This reads as a leftover, not-fully-updated year label carried over from an earlier edition of the same template rather than a deliberate date choice; correcting only the `date` field's year (while leaving every printed word of each entry's own content untouched) preserves this schema's required ascending-date ordering and keeps `date` a genuine calendar Sunday, which the source's own printed year would not. Printed-vs-corrected years, for the record: Nov 30 / Dec 7 / Dec 14 / Dec 21 / Dec 28 printed '2026', corrected to 2025; Oct 18 / Oct 25 / Nov 1 / Nov 8 / Nov 15 / Nov 22 printed '2025', corrected to 2026.

Non-congregation prayer subjects (diocesan ministries, named intentions, general reflections with no specific congregation) are recorded as `category` subjects using the source's own full printed sentence as `name`, verbatim, including its own leading 'For' where the source has one -- following this corpus's existing Idaho precedent (episcopal-idaho-2026.json) for treating a full printed intercession sentence as a category name rather than manufacturing a shorter label.

Five entries (March 8, June 7, September 6, October 11, October 25) carry the source's own extended, one-time collect-style prayer running well beyond a single sentence ('Camp Stevens Sunday', 'For Gun Violence Prevention', 'For the care of all of creation', 'For Deacons throughout the Church', 'For migrants and all who minister to them'). Rather than putting the entire paragraph into `name`, the source's own short heading (the text before its own colon) is used as that category subject's `name`, and the full prayer text that follows is preserved verbatim in that subject's `note` field so no content is lost. Each prayer's own closing 'Amen'/'Amen.' punctuation is preserved exactly as printed -- some of the source's own prayers end with a trailing period, some do not.

The week of March 1, 2026 (Second Sunday in Lent) prints two near-identical lines back to back -- 'For all the presenters and participants in Leadership Academy at Trinity, Escondido' and 'For all the presenters and participants in Leadership Academy' -- the second missing only the location clause. This reads as a leftover draft line not removed when the entry was finalized, but both are preserved verbatim as separate category subjects per this corpus's rule against silently dropping source content.

'Clergy and people of Christ Church Coronado' (January 25) omits the comma the source otherwise consistently uses between a congregation's name and its place; parsed here as parish name 'Christ Church', place 'Coronado'. 'Clergy and people of St. Brigid's in Oceanside' (November 15, 2026) uses 'in' rather than a comma; parsed as parish name 'St. Brigid's', place 'Oceanside'.

The source's own Deacons prayer (October 11 entry) prints 'Christ's service' with a straight apostrophe, two sentences after printing 'Christ’s redemptive love' with the curly apostrophe used everywhere else in the source. Preserved exactly as printed in each case rather than normalized to match.

The week of March 22, 2026 (Fifth Sunday in Lent) has no separate 'Clergy and people of' congregation line; its sole subject names the Nightwatch youth event, with St. Bartholomew's, Poway mentioned only as that event's host location for the morning, not given its own weekly rotation entry that week.

May 24, 2026's source line joins its parish and a second subject into one sentence ('Clergy and people of St. Thomas of Canterbury, Temecula and the children and teachers of St. Thomas Preschool'), unlike the source's usual pattern of two separate sentences (compare August 9 and 16's 'The children and teachers of St. ... Preschool', each its own capitalized sentence). Split here into two subjects for consistency with this file's parish/category separation elsewhere; the second subject's name is kept lowercase ('the children and teachers of St. Thomas Preschool') exactly as it reads mid-sentence in the source, not capitalized to match the other weeks' phrasing.

The phrase introducing each week's named congregation varies across the source ('Clergy and people of', 'Clergy and people of:', 'For the clergy and people of', 'Leadership and people of'). This boilerplate is not part of the congregation's own name and is excluded from `name` consistently throughout, regardless of which variant introduces a given week.

Verified against the source's own rendered PDF pages (not only the linearized text extraction), per this corpus's standing rule: the document is a single-column layout with no multi-column interleaving risk, and every entry below was visually cross-checked against the rendered pages before this file was finalized.

St. Andrew’s
For Deacons throughout the Church
subjects.note: We pray for Deacons: Gracious God, we praise you for sending your Son Jesus Christ, who took on himself the form of a servant, and humbled himself, becoming obedient even to death on the cross. We praise you that you have highly exalted him, and made him Lord of all; and that, through him, we know that whoever would be great must be servant of all. Today we thank you for raising up among us faithful servants for the ministry of your Word and Sacraments, and especially those called to serve as deacons in your Church. We give thanks for all deacons, for their example in word and action, in love and patience, and in holiness of life. We thank you for your ministry of making Christ’s redemptive love known to us; for the ways they interpret the needs, concerns, and hopes of the world to us; for their proclamation of your Word; and for their leadership in our sacramental life. As your Son came not to be served but to serve, may our deacons continue to share in Christ's service, and come to the unending glory of him who, with you and the Holy Spirit, lives and reigns, one God, for ever and ever. Amen.

subjects.note: Lord Jesus, when you multiplied the loaves and fishes, you provided more than food for the body, you offered us the gift of yourself, the gift which satisfies every hunger and quenches every thirst! Your disciples were filled with fear and doubt, but you poured out your love and compassion on the migrant crowd, welcoming them as brothers and sisters. Amen
